## Specific strengths
- **note-1a401b4a585c03902f3c** End-to-end teardown check is isolated: A dedicated lifecycle test module checks HTTP shutdown, session state, lingering owner tasks, and shutdown-related log messages. Keeping this resource-lifecycle probe in its own module aligns with the CI configuration that runs transport modules in fresh processes. Evidence: [ev-365565ee63f9cff289581be9](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/tests/test_mcp_gateway_lifecycle.py#L1), [ev-a19b2bfbf103f87636788ad9](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/tests/test_mcp_gateway_lifecycle.py#L1), [ev-a2853e45f5b5d94a3b039163](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L187).
- **note-356198538966288d23f8** Lifecycle cases are named and separated: The tests exercise normal exit, body error, cancellation, startup failure, and cancelled startup as distinct cases. Separating these lifecycle paths makes the expected ownership and cleanup behavior easier to understand and maintain. Evidence: [ev-bff417466e99ae2dc18f6132](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/tests/test_mcp_gateway.py#L399).
- **note-5094bb03d2331f5e66d7** Upstream session scopes have a dedicated owner: The gateway lifespan starts a named owner task that enters and exits the upstream connection context, while the hosting lifespan signals it to stop and awaits its completion. Keeping context-manager entry and cleanup in the same task addresses the documented cancel-scope ownership concern and gives shutdown an explicit completion point. Evidence: [ev-aef6091118f408e4484eb257](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/slopsearx/mcp/gateway.py#L1), [ev-e18e69d9ae88e58bee70aa8a](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/slopsearx/mcp/gateway.py#L383).
- **note-7600f5b37592b514687b** Lifecycle ownership is isolated: The gateway lifespan delegates the upstream connection context to a named, dedicated owner task, while the connection context remains a separate helper. This makes the task that enters and exits upstream scopes explicit and keeps connection setup distinct from the gateway lifespan coordination. Evidence: [ev-aef6091118f408e4484eb257](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/slopsearx/mcp/gateway.py#L1), [ev-e18e69d9ae88e58bee70aa8a](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/slopsearx/mcp/gateway.py#L383).
- **note-cf60185398a6868df7b1** Lifecycle tests cover distinct exit paths: The tests exercise normal exit, an exception in the lifespan body, cancellation, startup failure, and cancellation during startup. These cases make the ownership and fail-closed lifecycle contract explicit across more than the normal shutdown path. Evidence: [ev-bff417466e99ae2dc18f6132](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/tests/test_mcp_gateway.py#L399), [ev-feab56302732c2ce7df30e47](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/tests/test_mcp_gateway.py#L1).
- **note-cff045af2fc2d2eeac60** Real HTTP lifecycle check compares gateway behavior with direct calls: The added lifecycle test compares tool counts and structured results from a direct remote client and the gateway, then checks shutdown state and lingering owner-task conditions. This provides a concrete static test design for both proxy compatibility and resource cleanup across the HTTP boundary. Evidence: [ev-365565ee63f9cff289581be9](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/tests/test_mcp_gateway_lifecycle.py#L1), [ev-a19b2bfbf103f87636788ad9](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/tests/test_mcp_gateway_lifecycle.py#L1).
- **note-e0e91567747d43dd5e26** Lifecycle tests included in isolated CI execution: The CI workflow adds tests/test\_mcp\_gateway\_lifecycle.py to its isolated test-module list. This makes the lifecycle test module part of the configured CI test sequence and gives it a fresh process, consistent with the workflow's stated handling of live loopback tests. Evidence: [ev-3bba055702b5c07b50fffcf9](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L1), [ev-a2853e45f5b5d94a3b039163](https://github.com/magnus919/SlopSearX/blob/ea944ec047a2f006d719571f67068bc3d0fa36df/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L187).
